== Biography ==
'''John Hutcheson in Gairbraid''' is the senior John whom Hill’s compiled history identifies as husband of Marion Wilson, also called Jarden, and father of the founders’ father Thomas Hutcheson. The existing profile mixes this senior identity with material belonging to his eldest son, also John. Its inherited birth about 1500, birthplace and early rental chronology remain unverified; no new vital date is proposed.<ref name="Hill1902p53">[https://archive.org/download/earlyrecordsofol00hill/page/n78.jpg W.H. Hill, The Early Records of an Old Glasgow Family (1902), printed p. 53]. Printed page visually inspected 13 November 2026; underlying charters and genealogical manuscripts not inspected.</ref>

Hill reports a charter of confirmation dated 19 November 1582 favouring John in Gairbraid, Marion Wilson aliter Jarden and their eldest son John. He separately calls [[Hutcheson-1647|Thomas Hutcheson]], father of George and Thomas the charitable founders, their younger son.<ref name="Hill1902p53" />

The eldest son John married Agnes, daughter of William Anderson of Stobcross and Janet Maxwell. Hill then distinguishes another John, husband of Janet Johnstone. The eldest John or his son John apparently conveyed Gairbraid, or its reversion, to nephew or cousin George Hutcheson by a contract or disposition dated 5 August 1600. The alternative actor and tentative wording are preserved; the three Johns must not be collapsed.<ref name="Hill1902p53" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Source conflict and profile identity hold — 13 November 2026 ===
The current profile identifies its subject as the senior John of Gairbraid and father of Thomas, but assigns Agnes Anderson as wife. Hill assigns Agnes to the eldest son John, making her Thomas’s sister-in-law, not his mother. Do not copy the imported [[Anderson-95451|Agnes Anderson]] maternal link to Thomas, or the senior John/Agnes spouse pairing, into another tree while this conflict is unresolved. This is a source-conflict hold on those captured/imported roles, not a new replacement attachment.

The exact attached father pair Hutcheson-1651 to Hutcheson-1647 remains uncertain, without an invented percentage: the historical parent clause is explicit compiled evidence, while the existing profile identity is mixed. No Marion profile or extra John has been created, and no merge or live relationship edit has been made. Search compatible existing Marion Wilson/Jarden identities and inspect the original 1582 charter (Hill’s footnote 3: Genealogical MSS. of Hills etc., No.5) and the 1881 Hospital history, pp. 5–6, before resolving the profile identities.

Hill separates earlier traditionary names, including another Thomas appearing 1555/infeft 1563, from the later progenitors he supports with charters. The earlier blanket statement that Thomas’s parentage rests only on local tradition is superseded by this inspected printed account. This does not turn the underlying charter into an inspected original.

=== Historical captured account — retained for comparison, not current conclusions ===
The following full captured text is retained as the earlier unreviewed account. Its Agnes-as-wife, 1581 sasine, 1536 inheritance and generation/date assertions are not independently endorsed and are subject to the conflict above.

=== Earlier biography ===
'''John Hutcheson of Gairbraid''' was born around 1500 in the Glasgow area, Lanarkshire, Scotland. He is recorded as an early rentaller and landholder who established the Hutcheson family’s position at Gairbraid, a mile to the west of Glasgow, which would become the root of the family’s later estates and charitable legacy.

In 1536, John Hutcheson inherited part of the Gairbraid lands following the death of his father, according to local tradition. He appears in a sasine record from 1581 as "Johne Hutchesone sesing in the landis in Gairbraid," confirming his formal possession of the property. His wife at the time is recorded as Agnes Anderson.

The family’s status grew when, after the Scottish Reformation, old church annual rents were converted into feu-duties. This allowed the Hutchesons to become outright owners rather than tenants of Gairbraid. These lands, along with later acquisitions, formed the basis of the family’s wealth and influence in Glasgow for generations.

Through his son [[Hutcheson-1647|Thomas Hutcheson Sr.]] (born c. 1510–1520, died c. 1594), John is the direct ancestor of [[Hutcheson-1648|George Hutcheson (1554–1639)]] and [[Hutcheson-1650|Thomas Hutcheson Jr. (c. 1560–1641)]], the brothers who founded Hutchesons’ Hospital and Hutchesons’ School. These charitable institutions, along with properties like Lambhill, Hutchesontoun, and Gairbraid, formed the legacy that shaped the city’s history.

=== Earlier family ===
* Spouse: Agnes Anderson
* Father: ''[Unknown — probable rentaller of Gairbraid before 1536]''
* Children:
** [[Hutcheson-1647|Thomas Hutcheson Sr.]] (b. ~1510–1520, d. ~1594)

=== Earlier research notes ===
* First appears as a rentaller in 1536.
* Recorded in a sasine (1581) confirming possession of Gairbraid lands with Agnes Anderson as spouse.
* The Gairbraid estate later passed through his son Thomas to grandsons George and Thomas Jr., who expanded holdings at Lambhill and Hutchesontoun.

=== Earlier legacy ===
John Hutcheson’s work securing Gairbraid laid the foundation for the wealth that supported Glasgow’s greatest early charitable gifts: Hutchesons’ Hospital and School. Today, the area once part of the Gairbraid lands forms part of modern Maryhill.
